questions.a: It's the process of monitoring, responding to and acting on guest feedback across every location in a franchise network. Compared with a single restaurant, it means handling reviews at scale and keeping one brand voice across many operators. It also means spotting weak locations early so they don't hurt the whole brand.

questions.q: Why is reputation harder to manage for a franchise?
questions.a: You're handling reviews across dozens or hundreds of locations, each run by different operators. Keeping replies consistent and on-brand gets harder as you grow. One underperforming location can also drag down how guests see the entire brand.

questions.q: How do negative reviews affect a restaurant franchise?
questions.a: Negative reviews can stop guests from visiting, and a lower star rating often means lost revenue. In a franchise, a poor reputation at one location can spill over to the rest of the brand. That's why it pays to catch problems early and respond quickly.

questions.q: How can I keep a consistent brand voice in review replies across franchisees?
questions.a: Set shared response guidelines and manage replies from one central platform so every location follows the same tone. Corporate teams can provide templates and brand rules while still letting local teams handle their own guests. Reviewing replies regularly helps you catch locations that drift from the standard.

questions.q: How do I find which franchise locations are underperforming?
questions.a: Track ratings, review sentiment and recurring complaints for each location, then compare them side by side. Turning scattered feedback into network-level insights shows you where to step in before small issues grow. Proactive monitoring costs far less than reacting once a location's reputation has already slipped.
